correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs finite bridge coefficients as independent Wiener integrals against an orthonormal and complete cosine basis; variation of constants and Itô isometry give the exact full, infinite-error Parseval sum. Each coefficient is evaluated by an explicit exponential-cosine integral. Parity monotonicity and an exact derivative prove uniqueness and boundary optimality for all q>0. Summable Fourier weights and the odd-fourth-power series prove the small-q limits and finite-budget generalization. A supplied standalone standard-library verifier passed 127 independent numerical consistency checks; none is used instead of the analytic argument.

value.rationale: Finite Gaussian mode budgets are a genuine implementation constraint for smooth Brownian-bridge numerical SDE integrators. The theorem gives an exact, parameter-dependent optimal bridge-frequency selection, an unexpected bypass of the second harmonic, a sharp crossover, and an 84.11% asymptotic reduction in residual endpoint mean-square error at fixed cost. Its scope is clearly limited to strong OU endpoint coupling within a fixed sine basis; the result is not merely another arbitrary spectral table and does not pretend to outperform exact OU transition simulation.
